A feature release, and a break. The theme is **machines talking to each other
directly**. 0.4.2 and 0.4.3 reached a session on another computer by starting a
hidden Claude Code session and asking Anthropic's Remote Control to carry the
conversation — minutes per transcript, billed against your usage, and a relay
that had to be alive on both sides. That path is gone. Two machines on the same
network now pair once, keep a socket open, and the live view arrives in a
moment. Nothing signs into your account to do it.

Alongside that: an orb per Claude Code account that wears how much of it you
have spent, a chat panel whose text you can select and scale, typing into a
terminal that is not tmux, and a file on disk the next time the app crashes
instead of a day spent reproducing it.

Still a beta. Direct pairing is what this release is for, and the *Known
limitations* section is not boilerplate — read it before relying on a machine
you cannot see.

## New: pair two machines, and the live view is instant

**Settings → Other machines → Connect directly to other machines**, on both.
They find each other on the local network. Pair them once:

1. On one machine, press **Show a code**.
2. On the other, find that machine in the list and type the code next to its
   name. **Pair**.

The code is six digits, good for five minutes and one pairing. After that both
remember each other's certificate and reconnect on their own whenever both are
up. The first time it listens, macOS asks for Local Network access and Windows
raises a firewall prompt. Both of those are the feature working; a "no" here
looks exactly like the network being broken.

What you get is the live view 0.4.2 promised and delivered slowly: the other
machine's own conversation, verbatim, with scrollback, and what you type goes
into that session's input line so every slash command works. A chunk is no
longer 6 KB of base64 a model retypes; it is the whole transcript in one
message, and the deadline dropped from ten minutes to twenty seconds because
the ten minutes was measured against a model.

Two situations need a different route in, and both have one.

**A machine with no screen** — a Mac mini serving its sessions unattended — has
no button to press. Write the code into a file instead:

```bash
ssh your-mini
echo 123456 > "$HOME/Library/Application Support/ClaudeBuddy/pair-open"
```

Then pair from the machine that does have a screen. The file is read once and
deleted. A headless Mac can serve, but cannot *start* a conversation: macOS
gates the machine that opens a local connection, not the one that accepts it,
and a cupboard has nobody to approve the prompt. Pair from the machine with a
screen, add the headless one **by address**, and keep the connection up from
the laptop. One connection carries both directions.

**A machine this one cannot see** — another subnet, a VPN, a network that does
not carry the announcements — is **Add a machine by address**, with its address
and the code it is showing. Its name fills itself in once it answers.

Both machines still need Claude Buddy running. The far one no longer needs
Remote Control on, or a Claude account at all.

## Breaking: the Remote Control relay is gone

The hidden Claude Code session that used to carry this — the tmux pane named
`claude-buddy-rc-…`, the idle timer, the "Start serving at launch" switch, the
tray item **Connect to other machines** — is not in this build. 6,734 lines of
it came out.

Three things that means, in the order they will surprise you:

- **A session on a machine that is not on this network is no longer an orb.**
  The hotel case, the phone case, "I left a laptop at home and I am in a diner"
  — those were Anthropic's relay, and they left with it. Pairing is local.
- **A leftover relay is still running on a machine you upgrade.** Nothing in
  this app will ever start another, but the ones already in tmux keep sitting
  there, signed in, until you kill them. The app filters them so they do not
  become orbs (a session you never started, named after an internal mechanism).
  They still spend your usage until they die:

  ```bash
  tmux ls | grep claude-buddy-rc
  tmux kill-session -t claude-buddy-rc-<account>
  ```

- **A remote session not running under tmux can be listed and read, but no
  longer written to.** Typing needs an input line; the relay's messaging
  channel was what answered when there wasn't one. The panel says so rather
  than offering a composer that swallows what you type.

Settings keys for the relay are ignored. The Other machines card is the pairing
card and nothing else.

## New: usage orbs for each account (off by default)

If you run more than one Claude Code account, the only way to see how much of
each one you have spent used to be `/usage` in a session on that account. Turn
on **Usage orbs for each account** in Settings and each account gets an orb
instead.

Each orb wears three rings. Outside in: **this week** (the 7-day window),
**this session** (the 5-hour window), and **extra usage**. Colour is headroom,
not identity — green under 60%, amber to 85%, red above — so an account you do
not need to think about is a quiet green outline and a row of them reads from
across the room. Which account an orb *is* stays where it always is: the two
letters in the middle.

Hover for the numbers, the reset times and the extra-usage position. Click to
pin the card; pin two and they sit side by side. The orbs drag like the session
ones.

A window that has reset is not drawn. Extra usage that is genuinely off is a
dotted outline, not a gauge at zero; extra usage whose monthly limit is
**reached** is a full ring, because you have spent it. The card never guesses
why: it only says "switched off" or "limit reached" when the API states those
as facts. An earlier draft translated one other reason into "your organisation
disabled extra usage", which was not what had happened.

The numbers come from Claude Code itself, once every five minutes per account,
over the same control protocol its SDK uses. **It costs no tokens** — no model
call — and **nothing here reads a credential**. An account signed in with an
API key, or running against Bedrock or Vertex, has no subscription windows; its
orb says so rather than showing zeros.

## New: the chat panel is text, not a picture of text

**Selectable.** A reply can be selected and copied. The menu that used to live
only on the header is built with the panel.

**Scalable.** The panel's text grows the way every other app's does — the OS
setting, not a slider of our own.

**Opens at the newest message**, not wherever the last panel happened to be
scrolled. A capture in the screenshot suite photographs which end you land on,
because this is the kind of thing that looks fine in a unit test and wrong on
screen.

## Fixed: typing, naming, and orbs that told the truth

- **Type into a terminal that isn't tmux.** A local session running in a plain
  terminal, or a background job that has no terminal, now has a send path on
  every platform rather than a composer that claimed there was no terminal
  when the terminal had merely refused. One phrase for "can't type here".
- **Conversations, not processes.** One orb per session, not one per transport
  and not one per pid. A machine serving other machines reports the sessions it
  *has*, not the ones it happens to be drawing. Two peers with the same name
  are addressed by a ref, not guessed.
- **This machine is called what macOS calls it.** A Mac mini that DHCP had
  named `avatar.internal` was introducing itself as "avatar". Pairing keys off
  that name, so a word its owner had never chosen was the thing they were
  being asked to trust.
- **A self-updated Claude Desktop clone is repainted, not rebuilt.** Re-cloning
  over a bundle the updater had just replaced was the thing that silently
  moved a profile onto Default; detecting the drift was 0.4.3, repairing the
  icon without touching the bundle is this.
- **A crash writes itself down.** Unhandled exceptions go to
  `~/Library/Logs/ClaudeBuddy/crash.log` (macOS) or
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ClaudeBuddy\Logs\crash.log` (Windows), on by default. The
  next one costs a `cat` instead of a day.

## Fixed, smaller

- A send with no pane to type into takes the long way round rather than
  vanishing.
- The panel asks the client it actually has, not a stand-in.
- macOS Local Network refusal is named as the reason a gateway or a peer is
  unreachable, instead of looking like the host is down. `ping` and `curl`
  will still tell you it is fine — they are Apple-signed and exempt from the
  gate.
- The extra-usage card no longer claims an organisation disabled it when the
  month's budget is what ran out.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.0-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.0-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.0-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `ClaudeBuddySpeech-0.5.0-beta-*.zip` assets are the optional high-quality
voice engine. **You do not download these yourself** — the app fetches the
right one when you turn the setting on. They are published here because that is
where it looks.

The .NET runtime is bundled; nothing else is needed. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers
every file — verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` on macOS or
`Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows.

## Upgrading from 0.4.3-beta

**macOS**: replace the app in Applications. The signing identity is unchanged,
so Automation permission and click-to-focus carry over.

**Local Network permission does not.** Replacing the app gives it a new CDHash,
macOS re-evaluates Local Network access against it, and the grant does not
carry over. Anything on the LAN — paired machines, an OpenClaw gateway —
starts failing with `No route to host` and nothing prompts loudly enough to
notice. Approve it again in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local
Network. A headless Mac cannot approve it at all; pair from the machine with a
screen and add the headless one by address, same as first run.

**Windows**: run the new setup over the old one; it upgrades in place and
leaves your hook configuration alone.

Then:

1. **Kill leftover relays** if `tmux ls` still shows `claude-buddy-rc-…`.
   They will not die on their own and they still spend usage.
2. **Turn on Connect directly** on each machine you want in the picture, pair
   them, and say yes to the Local Network / firewall prompt.
3. **Restart any open sessions.** Hooks are read once at session start.

Relay settings (`remoteControlEnabled` and friends) are ignored and can be
deleted from `settings.json` whenever you like; they do nothing.

## Installing fresh

**macOS** — open the DMG, drag Claude Buddy to Applications, then double-click
**Install Claude Code Hooks.command**. Launch from Applications; nothing appears
in the Dock and no window opens, which is correct — look in the menu bar.

**Windows** — run the setup. Per-user, so no UAC prompt. Leave both checkboxes
ticked; tick **"Wire hooks for Claude Code running inside WSL"** too if you use
it.

### The hook step is not optional

Claude Buddy learns about your sessions from a hook that Claude Code (and, for
Codex sessions, Codex) runs. Until it is wired in, the app starts and runs
correctly and shows **nothing at all**. The installers offer to wire it up; let
them. Existing settings are backed up first, and re-running repairs rather than
duplicating.

## Known limitations

- **Direct pairing is local.** A machine that is not on this network is not an
  orb. The Remote Control path that used to cover a hotel or a phone is not in
  this release and is not coming back as a fallback — a quiet fallback onto a
  model-rewritten transcript is the thing this transport exists to refuse.
- **A headless Mac serves, but cannot dial.** Measured on a real Mac mini:
  `peer-connect-failed` and `discovery-announce-failed` are the same missing
  Local Network grant. Pair from the machine with a screen, add the mini by
  address, keep the connection up from the laptop. Screen-share into the mini
  once if you want it to dial as well; that is a one-time prompt.
- **Local Network consent is lost on every upgrade.** Same CDHash rule as
  Automation, and the failure is quieter — `ping` agrees with the wrong answer.
- **A remote session without tmux is read-only.** The panel says so.
- **Usage orbs read an experimental Claude Code response.** If the shape
  changes, the orbs go quiet rather than showing something wrong. Confirmed
  against a real account on macOS; Windows is the same protocol and has not
  been watched live.
- **The peer link has run on two real Macs**, including a headless mini, which
  is the setup this was built for. Windows has the same Settings card on both
  CI screenshot rids and has not been paired on two real Windows machines.
- **Windows installers are unsigned** — SmartScreen warns; choose **More info →
  Run anyway**. macOS builds are signed and notarized and open normally.
- A session killed with Ctrl+C at a permission prompt can still leave its orb
  stuck on amber. Right-click → *Reset this session to idle* clears it.

`docs/remote-control-findings.md` is the record of the path this release
deletes; the pairing, headless, and Local Network behaviour above was measured
on the same two machines that document lived on.
